result.memory: None built-in — OpenCode ships no auto-memory, memories dir, or MEMORY.md convention (no such page exists in its docs and no memory code exists in the repo); persistent cross-session memory is only available via third-party plugins such as opencode-supermemory, with OpenCode's own cross-session context being manually maintained AGENTS.md / ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md rules.
result.notes: Compatibility posture: OpenCode treats Claude Code as a first-class fallback at both tiers — project CLAUDE.md and global ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md for instructions, .claude/skills (project + global) for skills — each disabled individually via OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT / _SKILLS (or wholesale via OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE). It also reads .agents/skills (agent-compatible convention) and a deprecated CONTEXT.md. Nothing from Gemini/Cursor/Crush/Kilo is auto-loaded; Cursor/Copilot files enter only if a user lists them in opencode.json's instructions (docs example: ".cursor/rules/*.md") or remote https URLs (5s timeout). Config knobs mirror this: .opencode and ~/.config/opencode use plural subdirs (agents/, commands/, skills/, tools/, themes/) with singular names kept for backwards compatibility. Skill name collisions are not documented to resolve by precedence — docs demand globally unique names, while source effectively lets later scans overwrite earlier ones (config/.opencode dirs load after .claude/.agents, so native dirs win ties); a built-in "customize-opencode" skill is registered first and can be overridden by any disk skill. Instruction discovery is also lazy: reading a file in a subdirectory attaches that directory's nearby AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/CONTEXT.md up to the project root, once per message (Instruction.resolve in source). All evidence fetched during research from anomalyco/opencode (default branch dev, matches live opencode.ai/docs).

result.memory: Built-in learned memory: yes — "auto memory", on by default in local sessions, where Claude writes its own notes (types user/feedback/project/reference) per repository into ~/.claude/projects/<project>/memory/ (entrypoint MEMORY.md, first 200 lines or 25KB loaded into every session; shared across worktrees; relocated via autoMemoryDirectory, toggled via autoMemoryEnabled in ~/.claude/settings.json or CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1), and subagents can keep their own persistent memory in agent-memory/<name>/MEMORY.md.
result.notes: Compatibility: Claude Code now reads AGENTS.md natively (v2.1.277+), by default only when no CLAUDE.md/CLAUDE.local.md exists in the working directory or above; /config "Project instructions" (or pluginConfigs "agents-md@builtin" in user/managed settings) can set claude-md-and-agents-md to read both, claude-md, or managed-only. It does NOT read AGENTS.local.md, AGENTS.override.md, .agents/, GEMINI.md, CRUSH.md, .cursorrules, opencode.json, or kilo.jsonc as instructions. Interop paths: put @AGENTS.md (or @GEMINI.md etc.) in a CLAUDE.md, or symlink (Edit/Write refuse to write through a symlink); /init reads other tools' files (Cursor .cursor/rules/ + .cursorrules, Copilot .github/copilot-instructions.md, and with CLAUDE_CODE_NEW_INIT=1 also AGENTS.md, .devin/rules/, .windsurf/rules/ or .windsurfrules, .clinerules), and /import (v2.1.213+) copies another agent's config including MCP servers, commands, subagents and skills. Skills follow the open Agent Skills standard (agentskills.io, cross-tool SKILL.md) and custom commands were merged into skills (.claude/commands/ still works). Precedence: memory files are all concatenated (broadest to most specific: managed -> user -> project -> local; within a tree, root down to cwd with the cwd-closest read last); skill name collisions resolve enterprise > personal > project, skill beats a same-named command file, plugin skills are namespaced so they coexist, and nested skills coexist with root skills. Loading can be restricted by strictPluginOnlyCustomization, --safe-mode, or bare mode; Cowork and cloud sessions don't read the machine's ~/.claude/skills/ (they use claude.ai account skills); CLAUDE.md from --add-dir directories loads only when CLAUDE_CODE_ADDITIONAL_DIRECTORIES_CLAUDE_MD=1, and AGENTS.md from added directories never loads that way. Settings files (settings.json, managed-settings.json, .mcp.json) are configuration, not instruction/context files, and are covered by separate precedence (managed > CLI flags > user/local/project).

result.notes: Compatibility and extras. (1) Gemini CLI fork heritage: it no longer loads GEMINI.md as context — the filename constants are now QWEN.md/AGENTS.md (only deprecated setGeminiMdFilename aliases remain in code); CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md appear only in permission-classifier prompt text and stale comments, not in any loader. No .cursorrules / CRUSH.md / opencode.json / kilo.jsonc support. (2) Claude Code interop exists but not via convention files: `/import-config` imports MCP servers from ~/.claude.json and .claude/settings.json (packages/cli/src/config/claudeMcpImport.ts); the extension system consumes Claude's `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` + plugin.json and rewrites `.claude` path references to `.qwen`; subagent frontmatter mirrors `.claude/agents/*.md` verbatim so CC agent files can be copied into `.qwen/agents/` (project, highest precedence) or `~/.qwen/agents/` (user fallback); hooks accept CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR. It does NOT read ~/.claude/skills/ or .claude/skills/. (3) The shared `.agents` convention is honored for skills only — provider config dirs are ['.qwen','.agents'] at both user and project level; .agents is not used for rules/context. (4) Skills precedence: within a level the first provider dir wins, so .qwen beats .agents; across levels project > user > extension > bundled (documented in skills.md). A skill colliding with a custom command loses on the slash surface (commands load after skills). (5) Other instruction-ish files it loads: .qwen/agents/*.md and ~/.qwen/agents/*.md (subagent definitions), .qwen/commands/*.md and ~/.qwen/commands/*.md (custom slash-command prompts), .qwen/workflows/*.js surfaced as slash commands. Context files support @path/to/file.md imports (Claude-style import processor). (6) context.includeDirectories / context.loadFromIncludeDirectories can extend the QWEN.md scan across extra directories; QWEN_CODE_MEMORY_* env vars relocate/partition auto-memory.

result.notes: Compatibility: Crush deliberately reads other vendors' convention files — Claude (CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, ~/.claude/skills), Cursor (.cursorrules, .cursor/rules/, .cursor/skills), Gemini (GEMINI.md/gemini.md), GitHub Copilot (.github/copilot-instructions.md) — plus its own crush.md/CRUSH.md/*.local.md and the cross-tool AGENTS.md + Agent Skills spec (~/.agents/skills, SKILL.md folders, agentskills.io). No precedence/override among context files: every matching file is read and concatenated (project files in a "Project-Specific Context" block, global files in a "User context" block of the same system prompt); paths are alphabetically sorted and deduped, dirs under a context path are walked recursively, and ~/env vars are expanded. Context files are only looked up in the working dir (plus explicit context_paths) — unlike config files, which walk up from cwd and stop at the git worktree root so a stray crush.json above the repo is ignored. Config precedence is documented: project overrides global; in a directory .crushrc > crushrc > .crush.json > crush.json; /etc/crush/crush.json is lowest. crush.json is deprecated in favor of executable bash crushrc. `crush init` is only offered when no default context file already exists in the working dir; it writes initialize_as (default AGENTS.md) and then that file is read as a normal project context file. Builtin skills are embedded in the binary (internal/skills/builtin), user skill discovery honors $CRUSH_SKILLS_DIR as a full override of the global default dirs, and skills are deduplicated with working-dir versions taking precedence over git-root ones.
